title: Sell-with-simulators-mini-deck-draft
content:
Overview:
This is a compact slide deck (8–10 slides) + SE speaker notes for using interactive inference simulators during early technical qualification and pilot discovery. The aim is to give sellers a low-friction, repeatable way to demonstrate:
- realistic latency and token-cost tradeoffs for customer prompts
- how batch size, prompt truncation, and caching affect unit economics
- fallback routing and canary behaviors when capacity changes
- private vs hosted deployment decision signals

Intended audience:
- Sales Engineers (SEs) running 20–40min technical qualification calls
- Platform-focused AEs when discussing pilot shape and capacity

Slide-by-slide (speaker notes / what to demo):
1) Title + TL;DR (30s)
- Slide: Sell with Simulators — quick demo to de-risk pilot economics
- Note: 1-sentence value prop: we show predictable latency & cost in <10 minutes using live simulator profiles.

2) Why a simulator? (1 min)
- Slide bullets: 
  • Converts abstract claims into measurable numbers
  • Surfaces integration friction early (prompt length, throughput patterns)
  • Enables rapid canary scenarios and fallback rehearsals
- Note: quick anecdote — "platform team re-shaped batch config and saved 22% token cost in pilot"

3) Quick setup checklist (30s)
- Slide: 3 things we need: example prompts, target QPS, success metric (latency percentile or token cost ceiling)
- Demo note: ask customer to paste 2 representative prompts in chat now (or use provided anonymized prompts).

4) Simulator controls (2 min)
- Slide: controls UI: model variant, seq length cap, batch size, caching on/off, quantization mode, route (hosted/dedicated/private)
- Demo note: flip controls live to show delta in p95 latency and per-request token cost estimate.

5) Demo scenario A: Low-latency interactive UI (4 min)
- Slide: baseline: small prompts, p95 target < 120ms; show hosted model variant vs quantized dedicated
- Demo steps: run prompts at 5 QPS, show latency chart and cost burn. Turn on small batch size -> p95 jumps; turn on KV caching -> p95 drops.
- Talking points: "You can see small changes to batching/caching change cost by XX% without changing model outputs."

6) Demo scenario B: High-throughput background job (4 min)
- Slide: bulk embedding / summarization workload; show throughput vs cost curve, autoscale points
- Demo steps: ramp QPS to 200, show autoscaling thresholds, show fallback to cheaper region variant and graceful degradation logs.
- Objection script: if they say "we need predictable SLAs" -> highlight dedicated capacity option + simulator can project SLA attainment.

7) Quick interpretive heuristics (1 min)
- Slide: rules of thumb captured from platform tests:
  • If median seq length < 64 and QPS < 10, hosted + small batch is usually cheapest
  • KV caching is high-impact for repeated context patterns (FAQ/chat)
  • Long-tail latency sources: remote KMS, private VPC egress — flag these in pilot scoping

8) Try-it-yourself kit + next steps (1 min)
- Slide: links and call to action: "Run a 10-min sim with us — we’ll pre-fill your prompts and correlate to pricing estimate."
- Note: attach link to sandbox + pre-configured scenario for common verticals (support, search, summarization)

Appendix (SE quick reference notes):
- Demo runbook (checklist):
  1. Confirm network: is customer behind strict proxy/VPN? (affects private testing)
  2. Collect 3 canonical prompts and 1 spike pattern (burst QPS sample)
  3. Baseline run (no caching, default batch) -> capture p50/p95/cost
  4. Toggle caching and small batch changes -> capture deltas
  5. Show route fallback to compact model variant (note any quality trade)
  6. End with recommended pilot config and follow-up ticket

- Quick rebuttals / scripts:
  • "Simulator doesn't reflect our real data" -> "We run your exact de-identified prompts to avoid leakage; results are conservative because we use typical customer latencies and tokenization metrics."
  • "We can't share prompts" -> "We can use canonical prompts from the vertical kit and re-run with synthetic variations that mimic your workload."
  • "Cost numbers look optimistic" -> "Simulator emits cost estimates tied to our current price sheet; we'll run a small pilot and provide a contract-backed forecast."

- Known limitations / TODOs (notes to self):
  • Export-to-CSV for session metrics missing (JIRA-UX-223)
  • Need a one-click private-VPC toggle for in-office SEs (blocked on infra ticket INFRA-679)
  • Add anonymization checklist for sensitive prompt handling (ask legal)

Operational playbacks & metrics to capture post-demo:
- Capture: demo session id, prompts used (hashed), p50/p95 baseline, delta after changes, recommended pilot config (model + batch + cache + route), follow-up owner
- KPI for success: pilot conversion rate within 30 days; typical bench: 45–55% if simulator run + pilot offer is used vs 20–30% cold outreach

Handy snippets for email follow-ups (copy/paste):
- Short: "Thanks — attached are the 10-min simulator results. Key wins: p95 from 260ms -> 110ms with cache; projected token cost delta -18%. Recommend 30-day pilot on dedicated-small."
- Long: 3 bullets + link to replay + onboarding checklist + ask for POC access to test dataset

Slack/Confluence links to share with customer during call:
- Sandbox: https://sandbox.redwood.ai/sim-session?prefill=se-kit
- Replay: (placeholder after run)

Open questions (for product/infra):
- Can we make cost-estimates reflect reserved capacity pricing tiers dynamically? (ask pricing eng)
- Is there a safe default for anonymizing prompts that legal signs off on?
- Should we expose a "pilot-ready" button that creates reserved capacity estimate and brief SOW?

Notes to product: include a short A/B test to measure downstream pilot conversion lift when SEs run simulator vs. those who do not. Minimal instrumentation: flag in CRM when simulator used; check pilot conversion after 30 days.

Notes to engineering: prioritize CSV export and private-VPC toggle; small UX polish: show tokenized prompt length next to raw prompt.

End of draft.

(Informal: lots of shorthand here — this is a working draft for the SE playbook / 8-slide deck. Need UX mockups from Design, and a 2-slide legal blurb for handling PII. — Elena)
